pages.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF DELHI AT NEW DELHI
W.P.(C) 4125/2024 & CM APPL. 16890/2024

Meera Sharma                                         ...Petitioner
Versus
Union of India & Director General of Health Services ...Respondents

CORAM:
HON'BLE THE ACTING CHIEF JUSTICE MANMOHAN
HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE MANMEET PRITAM SINGH ARORA

ORDER
22.03.2024

1. The present writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been instituted seeking directions to respondents to ensure equitable access to essential life-saving therapies.
2. The petitioner is a 24-year-old resident of Delhi diagnosed with a rare metabolic disorder requiring lifelong enzyme replacement therapy.

3. It is stated in the petition that the cost of the imported therapy is prohibitively expensive, exceeding Rs. 40,00,000/- per annum, which is far beyond the financial capacity of the petitioner's family.

4. The petitioner submitted representations dated 14th November 2023 and 10th January 2024 to the Directorate General of Health Services under the National Policy for Rare Diseases, 2021 seeking financial assistance.
5. Despite the lapse of several months and urgency of the clinical condition, no formal decision has been communicated to the petitioner.
6. Learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner submitted that delay in administrative decision-making in matters involving critical medical treatment jeopardizes the very life of the petitioner.
7. Reference was made to the decision of this Court in Master Arnesh Shaw v. Union of India, W.P.(C) 5315/2020, wherein directions were issued for continuous funding of rare disease treatments.

8. Learned Central Government Standing Counsel appearing for respondent no. 1 and respondent no. 2 submitted that the representation of the petitioner is under active consideration of the Technical Committee.
9. It was submitted that financial disbursement under the National Policy involves coordination with designated Centers of Excellence across the country.
10. Learned Standing Counsel sought six weeks' time to complete the administrative evaluation and place a status report before this Court.
11. In response, counsel for the petitioner submitted that any further delay of six weeks would cause irreversible clinical deterioration to the petitioner.
7. The right to health is an integral facet of the right to life guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution.

12. The state has a constitutional obligation under Article 21 and Article 47 to preserve human life. Bureaucratic red-tape cannot be permitted to defeat constitutional guarantees in life-and-death medical situations.

8. The writ petition is accordingly disposed of with a direction to respondent no. 2 to decide the pending representation within four weeks from today by passing a reasoned and speaking order in accordance with law.

case_type.reasoning: The petitioner seeks a writ of mandamus under Article 226 of the Constitution to enforce public duty.

statutes.evidence: writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India

outcome.detail: The High Court disposed of the writ petition with directions to the respondents to decide the petitioner's representation within four weeks.
outcome.evidence: The writ petition is accordingly disposed of with a direction to respondent no. 2 to decide the pending representation within four weeks

key_dates.event: High Court order issuing directions on representation

record.summary: The Delhi High Court disposed of a writ petition filed under Article 226 seeking healthcare directions against public authorities. The Division Bench directed the Director General of Health Services to decide the pending representation in an expedited manner within four weeks. The court emphasized that timely administrative consideration is essential to uphold the right to health under Article 21.
record.summary_hi: दिल्ली हाईकोर्ट ने स्वास्थ्य सेवाओं के संबंध में दायर याचिका का निपटारा करते हुए स्वास्थ्य सेवा महानिदेशक को चार सप्ताह के भीतर लंबित प्रतिवेदन पर निर्णय लेने का निर्देश दिया है। अदालत ने कहा कि अनुच्छेद 21 के तहत स्वास्थ्य के अधिकार के लिए समय पर प्रशासनिक निर्णय आवश्यक है।

brief.facts: Petitioner, a patient requiring specialized treatment for a rare disease, submitted representations to health authorities for financial assistance under the National Policy for Rare Diseases 2021, which remained unconsidered.
issues: Whether a writ of mandamus lies to compel authorities to decide statutory financial assistance representations in an expedited timeframe under Article 21?
brief.arguments: Petitioner argued that indefinite administrative delay in rare disease treatment violates the right to health under Article 21. Union submitted that high-cost rare disease applications require scrutiny by the designated Center of Excellence.
brief.reasoning: The right to health is an integral part of the right to life under Article 21. Administrative authorities cannot sit indefinitely on medical representations requiring urgent intervention.
brief.decision: Writ petition disposed of with peremptory directions to decide representation within four weeks.
